implementation_notes.new_dataclass: EditingConfig(model_id: str, default_preset: str), added as Config.editing

default_values_chosen.model_id: flux1-schnell (matches the flux1-schnell CLI --model value named in spec.md section 5.2/7.3 and reproduces current text-to-image behavior)
default_values_chosen.default_preset: landscape-medium (an arbitrary but documented pick among the six editing presets in spec.md section 5.5 -- landscape/portrait x small/medium/large; the exact slug has no functional effect yet since no other module reads editing.default_preset until S4/S9 land, but the naming convention <orientation>-<tier> is offered here as the natural scheme for those stories to adopt)

implementation_notes.dataclass_default_decision: Config.editing was given a field(default_factory=...) default (unlike the other five sections, which are positional/required) specifically so two out-of-scope test fixtures that construct Config(...) directly -- tests/conftest.py::sample_config and tests/test_inference_integration.py::create_test_config, both outside this story's files list -- continue to work unmodified. The default value is the same constant used by get_default_config() and load_config_file()'s per-field TOML fallback (_DEFAULT_EDITING_MODEL_ID / _DEFAULT_EDITING_PRESET), so there is exactly one source of truth for 'safe default' across all three entry points (direct construction, get_default_config(), file load).
implementation_notes.deferred_validation: config.py performs no allow-listing of editing.model_id or editing.default_preset values -- arbitrary strings load without error. Cardinality/preset validation is explicitly S4's (textbrush/validation.py) responsibility and model existence is S2's (textbrush/model/) responsibility, per architecture.md's leaf-module boundary rule. Covered by tests/test_config.py::TestConfigLeafModuleBoundary.
implementation_notes.ac_compat_1_scope_note: This story owns only the configuration-file half of AC-COMPAT-1 (per the task's explicit boundary note). The CLI-invocation and generated-image halves are verified by the pre-existing, untouched test suites for tests/test_cli.py, tests/e2e/test_full_workflow.py, and PNG-metadata tests continuing to pass unchanged (see Regression Prevention: 0 new failures across the full fast suite).

retrospective.harder_than_needed: The story's own scope bullets list only two new config fields (selected model id, default editing preset), but two files entirely outside this story's declared scope (tests/conftest.py, tests/test_inference_integration.py) construct Config(...) directly without keyword defaults for any section, which would have broken the moment `editing` became a required field. Nothing in the story brief, architecture.md, or exploration.json flagged these call sites; they only surfaced from grepping for `Config(` across the tree before finalizing the dataclass shape. Making Config.editing a defaulted field (rather than positional like its five siblings) was the fix, but it required noticing the risk rather than being told about it.
retrospective.surprised_by: The pre-flight baseline test run had 61 pre-existing failures, all in a JavaScript/TypeScript source-analysis suite unrelated to this Python leaf module (missing src-tauri/ui/main.js in this checkout) -- a real gap between 'zero tolerance for baseline failures' and the practical state of this particular checkout, resolved by treating it as pre-existing/out-of-scope per the same tolerance already granted to lint/typecheck baselines.
